newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank of Italy says gold value set by EMI formula.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Italy says gold value set by EMI formula.

text.p: Italian gold reserves are already priced at close to market values, in line with a formula already approved by the European Monetary Institute (EMI), a source at the Bank of Italy said on Friday.
"The gold reserves will remain in their present conditions. There are already precise criteria for revaluations agreed at a European level with the EMI," the Bank of Italy source said.

Earlier this week, German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said he wanted Bundesbank gold and currency reserves to be revalued from current low book prices to levels close to the normal market price, in a bid to plug a hole in state accounts.
According to latest data from March, Italian gold reserves were worth 37.49 trillion lire against 39.54 trillion lire the same month last year.
At the end of 1996, the Bank of Italy held 1,504 tonnes of gold, with a further 518 tonnes lodged with the EMI -- the forerunner of the European central bank. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
